one_liner: Senior quality-control manager in the Intelligence Community Inspector General's audit office, checking that audits, inspections and evaluations meet GAGAS and CIGIE standards.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role requires at least 6 years in auditing, accounting, inspections or evaluations plus extensive knowledge of GAGAS and CIGIE inspection standards. Nothing on file shows Daniel has audit or evaluation experience, and the job also needs a TS/SCI-level clearance. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills fit the liaison and Congress-facing duties, but those are secondary to the technical audit core.
eligibility: Open to the public; this is an excepted service position, so Daniel can apply without federal status.
Mandatory: at least 6 years of experience in auditing or a related field such as accounting, inspections, or evaluations.
Mandatory: a bachelor's degree in accounting or a related field such as Business Administration, Finance, or Public Administration.
Requires Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access, so expect a lengthy background investigation and polygraph before starting.
Four free-response essays (200 words max each) must be written in your own words, with no consultant or AI help.
keywords: Quality Standards for Inspection and Evaluation
strategy: Before applying, honestly confirm whether your IEM work included program evaluation, compliance review, after-action reports or grant/FEMA Public Assistance documentation review; if it did not, skip this posting.

If the IEM work did involve reviews, frame it as evaluation work. Name the standards you worked under, such as FEMA policy, 2 CFR 200 or HSEEP, and describe how you reviewed evidence and documentation.
Count your years carefully. You need 6 or more years in auditing or a related field; state month/year dates and hours per week, and keep the resume to two pages.
Check that your degree major matches accounting, Business Administration, Finance or Public Administration, or a closely related field, and attach transcripts if required.
Write the four essays yourself, using concrete examples from emergency management work that show process improvement and how you carried out leadership direction you disagreed with.

Apply between Oct 15 and Oct 30, 2026. Better targets are GS-11/12 evaluation or analyst roles at FEMA, DHS OIG or Virginia's Office of the State Inspector General, which match your background more closely.
resume_bullets: Reviewed [number] [disaster recovery/grant] project files for compliance with [FEMA policy/2 CFR 200], identifying [issues] and recommending corrective actions adopted by [client].
Drafted [after-action reports/evaluations] for [government client], supporting findings with evidence from interviews, document review and observation across [number] stakeholders.
Served as primary liaison to [federal/state/local agencies], coordinating [reviews/deliverables] on [timeline] for a [$ amount] program.
interview_questions: How do you ensure a report's findings and recommendations are adequately supported by evidence?
Explain the key GAGAS requirements for a system of quality management.
Describe a time you had to deliver critical feedback on a colleague's work product.
How would you prepare an office for an external peer review?
watch_outs: The audit experience and GAGAS/CIGIE expertise are mandatory, so applying without them will likely fail basic qualifications.
The job requires SCI clearance, no telework, and a McLean commute from Manassas.
The application window is short: October 15 to 30, 2026.
